review_notes: Read the whole target file and compared it to Mathlib/Order/Nucleus.lean (range n as a Frame, Nucleus.restrict, Nucleus.giAux/giRestrict) and Mathlib/Order/CompleteSublattice.lean. Only Nucleus.lean and Sublocale.lean mention Sublocale. I found one well-supported finding: a parallel Frame/restriction/Galois-insertion development for `Sublocale`, duplicating the one for `range n`. I considered the overlap with CompleteSublattice (sInf-closure, top_mem, InfSet on the subtype) but did not report it: the structures differ because a sublocale is not sup-closed, the TODO in the file already acknowledges it, and no shared InfClosed-style predicate exists to integrate with. Uncertainty: the two Frame instances on the same underlying type might not be defeq. I did not check the exact defeq status, and I cannot compile.

findings.excerpt: def restrict (S : Sublocale X) : FrameHom X S where
findings.problem: Mathlib already has a complete development of the same concept for the range of a nucleus. `Nucleus.lean` defines a `Frame (range n)` instance, a private `giAux` Galois insertion, `Nucleus.restrict : FrameHom X (range n)` and `Nucleus.giRestrict`. This file redoes the same chain for `↥S`. It defines `restrictAux` via `sInf {s : S | a ≤ s}`, a `giAux`, a `FrameHom X S` and a `giRestrict`, and proves the frame-hom axioms by a long separate calc. A sublocale `n.toSublocale` has carrier `range n` (`Nucleus.toSublocale` uses `carrier := range n`), so `↥n.toSublocale` and `↥(range n)` are the same subtype of `X`. Despite that, there are two different `Order.Frame` instances and two different restriction frame homs, `Nucleus.restrict` and `Sublocale.restrict`. Nothing relates them. The only bridge, `Nucleus.restrict_toSublocale`, proves a bespoke statement by unfolding `Sublocale.restrict`. `Sublocale.restrict` also has a much heavier proof than `Nucleus.restrict`, whose `map_inf'` is `by ext; exact map_inf`.
findings.proposed_change: Make one of the two developments derive from the other, e.g. define the restriction through the nucleus-side API. Define `Sublocale.restrict S` via `S.toNucleus.restrict`, or prove `Sublocale.restrict` as a transport of `Nucleus.restrict` along `range_toNucleus`. Alternatively, define `Nucleus.restrict`/`giRestrict` for `range n` from `n.toSublocale`. At minimum, state and prove a lemma identifying `Nucleus.restrict n` with `n.toSublocale.restrict` (and the two Frame/CompleteLattice structures), so one proof of the frame-hom axioms and of the Galois insertion is reused. Drop `restrictAux`/`giAux`/`giAux` private duplicates and the long `calc` for `map_inf'`.
findings.benefit: It removes a second proof of the same frame-homomorphism and Galois-insertion facts, which currently takes about 40 lines. Users get one canonical restriction map and frame structure on the image of a nucleus instead of two non-interchangeable ones, so they no longer need ad hoc conversions between `range n` and `n.toSublocale`.

evidence.excerpt: @[simps] def restrict (n : Nucleus X) : FrameHom X (range n) where
def giRestrict (n : Nucleus X) : GaloisInsertion n.restrict Subtype.val := n.giAux
